c.tagline: Switzerland's storybook capital - a UNESCO medieval old town wrapped in a bend of the Aare.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered but expensive; ranks sit at the station and Barenplatz, or book by phone (Bara Taxi / Nova Taxi). Uber operates but with limited coverage, so a booked taxi is often faster.

emergency.note: 112 works as the general European emergency number; 117 reaches police, 144 ambulance, and 118 fire.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Altstadt (Old Town): Zytglogge clock tower Bern old town

avoid.reason: Minor pickpocketing around the train station and Old Town in summer, and the Schützenmatte/Reitschule area can feel edgy late at night.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed medieval core on the Aare peninsula - six kilometres of covered arcades (Lauben), the Zytglogge astronomical clock, the Bundeshaus, and the cathedral; where most visitors stay and everything is walkable.

An elegant, planned 19th-century quarter of Belle Epoque villas and embassies across the Kirchenfeldbrucke, home to Bern's densest cluster of museums including the Historical Museum with its Einstein Museum; refined and leafy.
The lively university quarter west of the station, with student cafes, bookshops, bakeries, and an unpretentious local feel; quieter than the old town but well connected.
Bern's bohemian, alternative neighbourhood just north of the river, known for street art, indie bars, the riverside Botanical Garden, and a young creative crowd.
A laid-back residential district northeast of the centre around Breitenrainplatz, with neighbourhood restaurants, the Rosengarten viewpoint nearby, and an easy local pace.

water.note: Tap water and the old town's public fountains are safe to drink.

transit.hours: Bernmobil trams and buses run from about 5:00 AM to midnight, with Moonliner night buses on weekends.
transit.note: Bernmobil runs the city trams and trolleybuses, tightly integrated with RBS/BLS S-Bahn regional trains through the Libero fare network. The compact UNESCO old town is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Buy from platform machines or the Bernmobil / FAIRTIQ app, or tap a contactless card; validate before boarding. Hotel guests receive a free Bern Ticket covering city zones for their stay.

car.idp: Not required for most foreign licences

train: Bern Hauptbahnhof (SBB InterCity to Zurich, Geneva, Basel; direct TGV Lyria to Paris)

transit.m: Bus + S-Bahn via Belp station to Bern centre (~25 min); most visitors instead fly into Zurich (ZRH), ~1h by direct train
Taxi to the city centre (~15-20 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up to the nearest franc or ~5% for good service is customary but not expected.

food.name: Berner Platte
food.desc: A groaning platter of smoked pork, beef, bacon, sausage and salted tongue with sauerkraut, beans and boiled potatoes; a two-person job at least.

places.name: Restaurant Della Casa
places.note: Bernese institution cooking the platter from recipes barely changed since the restaurant opened.

places.name: Kornhauskeller
places.note: Grand vaulted cellar under the old granary, one of the most atmospheric rooms in Switzerland.

places.name: Restaurant Harmonie
places.note: Family-run and packed with locals; has been the Bernese lunch spot for over a century.

food.name: Berner Rosti
food.desc: Grated potato pressed into a golden cake and fried in butter; the Bernese version is often crowned with bacon, cheese or a fried egg.

places.name: Kornhauskeller
places.note: Berner Rosti is among the most recommended plates in the historic cellar.

places.name: Restaurant Della Casa
places.note: Classic rosti served with game in season and with the Berner Platte year-round.

places.name: Altes Tramdepot
places.note: Brewpub in the old tram shed with rosti and river-and-Old-Town views.

food.name: Zibelechueche
food.desc: Bern's onion tart: sweet softened onions in a savoury custard on a short crust, tied to the November Zibelemarit onion market.

places.name: Restaurant Harmonie
places.note: Cooks the tart in season for a room full of regulars rather than tourists.

places.name: Kornhauskeller
places.note: Puts Bernese seasonal specialities including the onion tart on the menu each autumn.

places.name: Zibelemarit stalls on Bundesplatz
places.note: On the fourth Monday of November the whole centre sells onion tart and gluhwein from dawn.

food.name: Meringues mit Doppelrahm
food.desc: Crisp Swiss meringues buried under thick double cream from the Emmental valley; simple, extravagantly rich and unmistakably Bernese.

places.name: Restaurant Harmonie
places.note: The traditional finish to a Harmonie lunch, served with proper Emmental double cream.

places.name: Altes Tramdepot
places.note: Dessert menu keeps the meringue-and-cream classic alongside the house beers.

places.name: Restaurant Zum Goldenen Schlussel
places.note: Bern's oldest restaurant, a dependable place for the old-fashioned desserts.

food.name: Cordon bleu
food.desc: Veal or pork beaten thin, wrapped around ham and cheese and fried until it spills; a Swiss restaurant benchmark Bern takes seriously.

places.name: Restaurant Zum Goldenen Schlussel
places.note: The oldest restaurant in Bern, and its cordon bleu is the dish it is best known for.

places.name: Restaurant Harmonie
places.note: Traditional, generously sized version served to a loyal lunchtime crowd.

food.name: Mandelbarli
food.desc: Little almond-marzipan bears, a Bern-specific sweet nodding to the bear on the city's coat of arms.

places.name: Confiserie Eichenberger
places.note: The confectioner most associated with Bern's marzipan bears; boxes travel well.

places.name: Confiserie Tschirren
places.note: Long-established chocolatier on the arcaded main street with house pralines and marzipan.

food.name: Bernese craft beer
food.desc: Bern brews its own: Felsenau from the river bend below the city and Gurten named for the hill, plus brewpub lagers poured fresh.

places.name: Altes Tramdepot
places.note: Brews its own lager, amber and seasonal beers on site with a terrace over the Aare.

places.name: Kornhauskeller
places.note: Cellar bar pours Swiss beers under frescoed vaults; good for one drink even without dinner.

places.name: Restaurant Della Casa
places.note: Ground-floor stube is a proper local drinking room, beer and Bernese chatter.

food.name: Trasch and kirsch
food.desc: Swiss fruit eau-de-vie: kirsch from cherries, trasch from pears, taken as a small ice-cold digestif after a heavy plate.

places.name: Restaurant Della Casa
places.note: The classic way to finish a Berner Platte here, poured at the table.

places.name: Restaurant Zum Goldenen Schlussel
places.note: Keeps a range of Swiss fruit schnapps behind the bar.

places.name: Restaurant Harmonie
places.note: Old-school digestif service to match the old-school cooking.

landmarks: Zytglogge (Clock Tower)
Bern's medieval gate tower performs an hourly mechanical puppet show beneath its 1530 astronomical clock, the beloved centerpiece of the UNESCO-listed old town.
Bern Minster (Berner Münster)
Switzerland's tallest cathedral spire crowns this Gothic masterpiece, whose vivid Last Judgment portal and 312-step tower climb reward with Alpine panoramas.
Old Town Arcades (Altstadt)
Six kilometers of sandstone arcades, Renaissance fountains and cellar shops line the UNESCO old town, wrapped in a dramatic bend of the turquoise Aare.
Bear Park (BärenPark)
Bern's heraldic bears roam a terraced riverside enclosure below the old town, continuing a city tradition of keeping live bears since the sixteenth century.
Federal Palace (Bundeshaus)
Switzerland's domed parliament building lords over Bundesplatz, where a playful 26-jet fountain represents the cantons and free tours reveal the ornate assembly halls.
Rose Garden (Rosengarten)
Above the Bear Park, 200 varieties of roses frame the classic postcard panorama of Bern's medieval rooftops curled inside the Aare's loop.
Zentrum Paul Klee
Renzo Piano's three rolling steel waves rise from the fields east of town, sheltering the world's largest collection of works by Bern-raised painter Paul Klee.
Einstein House (Einsteinhaus)
The modest Kramgasse apartment where Albert Einstein developed his 1905 theory of relativity is preserved with period furnishings above the arcades he strolled daily.
Aare River and Marzili Baths
In summer, locals float the glacier-cool Aare downstream to the free Marzili lido, a beloved Bernese ritual with Bundeshaus views from the water.
Gurten
Bern's local mountain, reached by a red funicular, spreads picnic lawns, a lookout tower and grandstand views from the Alps to the Jura.

intl.to: Milan (Italy) - via the Lötschberg base tunnel

train.note: Bern Hauptbahnhof is right at the edge of the old town and is the hub of the Swiss network - Zurich in under an hour, Geneva in 1h45, Interlaken in 50 minutes. The direct TGV Lyria to Paris takes about four hours, and EuroCity services run through the Lötschberg tunnel to Milan. Swiss Supersaver fares open about two months ahead and are much cheaper than full price.

bus.note: Coaches use the stop at the Neufeld park-and-ride on the northern edge, reached by tram 9, rather than the central station. FlixBus covers the European routes; within Switzerland the train network is so dense that intercity coaches barely exist. PostBus (https://www.postauto.ch/en) fills the gaps to mountain villages.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry in Bern - the Aare loops around the old town and is famous for summer swimming and drifting rather than boats. BLS lake boats operate on Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, about an hour away by train, and are covered by Swiss rail passes.

half.name: Thun
half.blurb: A town at the mouth of Lake Thun with a hilltop castle overlooking the water and the Bernese Alps beyond.

half.name: Fribourg
half.blurb: A bilingual medieval town straddling a river gorge, its old town linked by covered wooden bridges and steep stairways.

half.name: Interlaken
half.blurb: A town wedged between two lakes in the Bernese Oberland, the main gateway for trips into the high Jungfrau alpine region.

full.name: Lucerne
full.blurb: A Swiss lake town beneath snow-capped peaks, known for its covered wooden Chapel Bridge and views toward Mount Pilatus.

full.name: Gruyères
full.blurb: A walled hilltop village in the Fribourg Alps famous for the cheese that bears its name, with a medieval castle at its center.
